title: TRACE: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Reasoning Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.24232v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) generate intermediate reasoning traces that may contain unsafe content, even when their final responses appear safe. Guardrail models are designed to detect and block unsafe content, yet existing benchmarks for unsafe content detection focus primarily on prompts and final responses, leaving reasoning traces largely unexamined. Moreover, these benchmarks typically provide only binary safety labels, without evidence annotations that justify the judgments. To address these limitations, we introduce TRACE, an evidence-grounded safety evaluation benchmark that covers the entire LRM inference pipeline: prompts, reasoning traces, and final responses. TRACE includes prompts in two languages spanning nine risk categories and ten attack strategies. translated_title: TRACE：面向大型推理模型安全评估的基于证据的基准
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24232v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大型推理模型（LRMs）会生成中间推理痕迹，其中可能包含不安全内容，即使其最终响应看起来是安全的。护栏模型旨在检测和阻止不安全内容，但现有的不安全内容检测基准主要关注提示和最终响应，对推理痕迹的考察在很大程度上被忽视。此外，这些基准通常仅提供二元安全标签，而没有证明判断依据的证据注释。为解决这些局限性，我们引入了TRACE，一个基于证据的安全评估基准，覆盖了LRM推理管道的完整流程：提示、推理痕迹和最终响应。TRACE包含两种语言的提示，涵盖九个风险类别和十种攻击策略。对于每个提示，四个LRM生成推理痕迹和最终响应，我们注释每个组件的安全性，并从相应内容中提取支持性证据。
tldr: TRACE是一个全新的基于证据的安全评估基准，它首次系统覆盖了大型推理模型的完整推理过程（提示、推理痕迹和最终响应），并提供了支持安全判断的证据注释，弥补了现有基准仅关注提示和最终响应且缺乏证据标注的不足。
en_tdlr: TRACE is a novel evidence-grounded safety evaluation benchmark that systematically covers the entire reasoning pipeline of large reasoning models (prompts, reasoning traces, and final responses) and provides supporting evidence annotations for safety judgments, addressing the gaps of existing benchmarks that focus only on prompts and final responses without evidence labeling.
